title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche, 1981). K is a field finitely generated over Q. E_K = Gal(K̄/K) sits in an extension 1 → π_K → E_K → Γ → 1. Here π_K = Gal(K̄/K·Q̄) is the geometric (birational) fundamental group, and Γ = Im(E_K → Γ_Q) is open in Γ_Q. B_K is the classifying topos of E_K. A morphism of topoi B_{K'} → B_K over B_Q is the same as an outer homomorphism E_{K'} → E_K compatible with the projections to Γ_Q.

On the previous page Grothendieck called such a homomorphism 'admissible' when the centralizer in the target of the image of every open subgroup is trivial. He also noted that a naive Hom-conjecture fails, since one does not want Γ-homs out of π_{K'} = 1 but sections.

The question-conjecture. Are the following equivalent?
- (a) The outer homomorphism comes from a field embedding K ⊂ K'.
- (b) E_{K'} → E_K has open image.
- (c) It is admissible.

The margin already warns: 'c) is not strong enough, see below'.

The NB records the easy implications a ⇒ b ⇒ c.
- a ⇒ b: K̄ ∩ K' is finite over K because K' is finitely generated, so the restriction image Gal(K̄/K̄∩K') is open.
- b ⇒ c: open subgroups of these Galois groups have trivial centralizers (the 'théorème 1' of the notes).
- Because everything is compatible with the maps to Γ_Q, (b) is equivalent to the induced π_{K'} → π_K having open image.

Consequence tested. 'degré' here means transcendence degree, i.e. dimension. Suppose trdeg K' < trdeg K. Then an open-image homomorphism is impossible, so a positive answer would forbid any admissible E_{K'} → E_K over Γ_Q. Take K' to be a number field k', so E_{K'} = Γ' is open in Γ. Then any section s : Γ' → E_K of E_K → Γ would have to be non-admissible: for some open Γ'' the centralizer of s(Γ'') in E_K is nontrivial. That centralizer maps into the centralizer of Γ'' in Γ, which is trivial, so it lies in π_K. Hence (if π_K ≠ 1) π_K^{s(Γ'')} ≠ 1.

Grothendieck then notices this is probably false, as the next page confirms. A section coming from a rational point lands in a decomposition group whose inertia is ≅ Ẑ(1)^d. Γ' acts on that inertia through the cyclotomic character, which gives no Γ'-fixed points. By contrast, the kernel Γ'^o of the cyclotomic character does fix it.

The fix on the next page:
- Replace (c) by (c'): admissibility tested on Σ^o_{K'} = ker(Σ_{K'} → Γ_Q → Ẑ^*).
- This needs the fact that centralizers of Γ'^o in Γ_Q are trivial.
- The corrected conjectural consequence: for every section over an open Γ' (with π_K ≠ 1), π_K^{Γ'^o} ≠ 1.

This amounts to an early group-theoretic prediction that birational Galois sections behave like decomposition groups of points, i.e. a weak form of the birational section conjecture.
errors: The deduction 'π_K^{Γ'} ≠ 1' is loosely stated. Non-admissibility only gives a nontrivial centralizer for SOME open subgroup Γ'' ⊂ Γ', so the conclusion should be π_K^{s(Γ'')} ≠ 1 for some open Γ''.

The conjecture as first stated (a ⇔ c) is false, as Grothendieck himself realises. For a section coming from a rational point, Γ' acts on inertia Ẑ(1)^d via the cyclotomic character; weight considerations suggest π_K^{Γ'} = 1 even for geometric sections, so (c) does not separate genuine embeddings from sections (points/places).
The NB as transcribed has 'π_K → π_{K'}'. The direction should be π_{K'} → π_K, consistent with E_{K'} → E_K; this is a slip in either the manuscript or the transcription.
'degré K'/Q' must mean transcendence degree. Read literally as a field degree it would be meaningless for transcendental extensions.

ideas.what: Hom-form of the birational anabelian conjecture: an outer Γ_Q-homomorphism G_{K'} → G_K comes from an embedding K ⊂ K' iff it has open image.
ideas.modern_name: Hom-version of the birational anabelian conjecture (open homomorphisms of absolute Galois groups of function fields)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, Letter to Faltings 1983 / Longue Marche); Isom form proved by Pop (1994); Hom/open-homomorphism forms by Mochizuki (1999, sub-p-adic setting) — attribution of the exact Hom statement unsure
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (in spirit); La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Admissibility = triviality of centralizers of images of open subgroups, used as a candidate criterion for 'geometric' homomorphisms; centre-freeness of open subgroups of Galois groups of finitely generated fields.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Neukirch–Uchida–Ikeda circle for number fields; 'slim' terminology Mochizuki

ideas.what: Observation that the condition must be tested on the kernel of the cyclotomic character (Σ^o), because decomposition groups of points contain inertia Ẑ(1)^d fixed by Γ'^o but not by Γ'.
ideas.modern_name: role of cyclotomic twist / inertia Ẑ(1) in characterizing decomposition groups; birational section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birational section conjecture: Grothendieck; work by Koenigsmann, Pop, Stix, Esnault–Wittenberg

ideas.what: Dimension monotonicity: no open-image Γ_Q-homomorphism G_{K'} → G_K if trdeg K' < trdeg K, applied to sections (K' a number field).
ideas.modern_name: group-theoretic characterization of dimension / sections vs. embeddings
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard consequence of cohomological dimension (cd π_K = 2·trdeg)

missed.claim: Conjectural consequence (with the next-page correction): every section of G_K → Γ_Q over an open Γ' has nontrivial fixed points in π_K under the kernel of the cyclotomic character. This is a purely group-theoretic weak birational section conjecture, phrased as 'π_K^{Γ'^o} ≠ 1' rather than 'the section is a decomposition group'.
missed.quote: cela impliquerait que pour de telles sections, on aurait (si π_K≠1) π_K^{Γ'}≠(1). Or je m'aperçois que [ceci est sans doute faux]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a weak, testable necessary condition for birational sections (fixed points under Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞))-type subgroups). This could be compared with Pop's and Koenigsmann's p-adic birational section results. As far as I know it is not singled out in the literature, though it follows from the birational section conjecture.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly records that the naive centralizer-admissibility criterion (c) fails to characterise geometric homomorphisms, and must be replaced by the stronger condition on cyclotomic kernels. This is a documented self-correction in the genesis of the Hom-conjecture.
missed.quote: c) n'est pas assez fort, cf plus bas...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for how the Hom-form (open image) became the accepted formulation over centralizer conditions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working draft of the birational Hom-conjecture, which is well known and largely proven. The mildly notable unpublished details are the explicit failure of the centralizer criterion and the cyclotomic-kernel refinement leading to a weak section-type prediction. These are interesting genesis details but not a lost result.
